newsitem.title: UK: Weather, currency rule week ahead on Euro veg oils.
newsitem.headline: Weather, currency rule week ahead on Euro veg oils.

text.p: Weather patterns in the U.S. midwest and the performance of the dollar are likely to rule the European vegetable oil market in the coming week.

The soft oil sector is expected to react slowly to any decrease in Chicago soy futures mainly due to the firm dollar while the upside of the market is limited by buyers reluctance to pay higher prices.
"Sellers can ask what they like, but at the end of the day they have to convince the buyers that the price is going to stick," said one trader.
Traders are watching the weather pattern in the U.S. Midwest where a hot dry weekend needs to be followed by rain to aid crop development.
U.S. forecasters were at odds over the weather pattern with some calling for widespread rain over the southern half of the corn belt while others expected closer to 50 percent coverage.
Palm oil is expected to trade lower in the coming week on a production driven market.
"The firm dollar has made palm oil look more attractive recently, but production worries are taking over again," said another trader.

In his latest crop report Malaysian private forecast Ivan Wong pegged output during July at 630,000 to 635,000 tonnes, while according to figures release by cargo surveyor SGS exports during the first 25 days of July were estimated at 580,610 tonnes.
"The palm oil market is looking at stocks in Malaysia of around one million tonnes soon," said on e trader.
Talk of a barter deal between Iraq and Malaysia was not seen as significant by European traders.
"We have not heard about this, but even if it's true it is unlikely to have much impact, if any, on the price of palm oil," said a trader.
"Around 20,000 tonnes of palm oil is being shipped to Iraq every month so I don't see what the excitement is all about," said one Singapore-based trader.

Coconut oil prices may bounce a little, but ample supplies at origin will continue to depress the market. However, lower prices could lead to Indonesia reducing exports which would trigger a rally in the longer term.
